title: Operational Health Initiative: cadence, gates, and visibility ledger
creator: Anika Patel
description: Goal: Build a lightweight, cross-team ledger and cadence that ties engineering initiatives to service health signals and automated release gates. The ledger will make visible the current health runway for each initiative, map initiative owners to health signals, and provide an enforced gating policy for rollouts when short-term health deterioration is detected. This work focuses on product-management surface area: roadmap integration, runbooks for gating decisions, and Console UX hooks for visibility. Engineering will deliver the signal feeds and gating API; Design will provide compact visualization patterns for the Console.
acceptance_criteria: Console dashboard shows initiative-level health ledger with 30/90-day runway and burn-rate indicator
A stable API and webhook that publishes initiative health state (green/amber/red) to release pipelines
Three pilot initiatives successfully use gating webhook to pause or throttle rollouts during high burn events
Runbook and playbook published in Confluence outlining decision thresholds and escalation path
Telemetry: per-initiative SLI aggregation and a daily digest report available to PMs and Eng leads
notes: Scope decision (2025-09-10): focus on availability/latency and request-throughput SLIs first; expand to correctness and downstream dependency SLIs in phase 2.

Trade-off: chose a compact 1-line health status (green/amber/red) for quick gating decisions rather than exposing all raw metrics in the first rollout. We will provide a drilldown link to full SLI charts.
Design feedback (2025-09-22): visualization needs an inline initiative owner badge and one-click mute for noisy infra signals. Designer: Mei Huang.
Engineering note (2025-10-01): initial API will accept aggregated SLI windows (1h, 6h, 24h) and compute a burn-rate score; longer windows deferred to phase 2. Implementer: ENG-20123.
Risk: potential for gating to block legitimate feature rollouts if downstream service flaps; mitigations include false-positive suppression rules and canary exemptions for infra-hotfixes.

Prioritization rationale: this increases confidence in launches across Dedicated and Private customers and reduces incident-driven rollbacks, aligning with Q4 OKRs for reliability and release velocity.
updates: 2025-09-05 - Kickoff: PM, Eng, Design aligned on scope and success metrics; formed pilot group (Search, Dedicate autoscaler, Console).
2025-09-18 - Design mockups delivered; consensus on compact ledger card and drilldown flow. Action: Design -> handoff to frontend by 2025-10-02.
2025-10-08 - Engineering spike completed: feasibility confirmed for 1h/6h/24h signal aggregation; initial webhook schema approved in API review (see PR #4821).
2025-10-22 - Pilot instrumenting: Search team integrated health webhook in canary pipeline; first canary paused automatically when availability burn exceeded threshold (test event).
2025-11-03 - Cross-team review: Security reviewed conduit for signal publishing; recommended scoped service account and audit logs (follow-up ticket ENG-20567).
2025-11-12 - Beta rollout: Console shows ledger for 6 pilot initiatives; collecting PM feedback on noise and thresholds.
2025-11-18 - Decision: widen visibility to Dedicated customers in December but keep auto-gating limited to internal builds until suppression rules mature.
open_questions: What should the default burn-rate threshold be for auto-gating across all services? Proposal: 7-day burn > 25% triggers amber; > 50% triggers red and gating.
How to represent multi-service initiatives where different SLI types have conflicting signals? Proposal: weighted health score by initiative service exposure (follow-up modeling required).
What exemptions are required for urgent infra patches to avoid gating? Devops proposed a special 'infra-hotfix' token to bypass gates.
